 Diwali is just round the corner, and the air is already filled with the sound of music and festivities; streets are lined with bright lights, and people are out there. But every year, as Diwali comes nears, the same question starts floating around family WhatsApp groups and among friends that when the big actually is? Is it today or tomorrow? Which day do we do the puja? One calendar says one date, a news website says another, and the pandit has a third opinion. It gets confusing all the more when we ask different set of people every time, and especially when you have a house to clean, sweets to order, and guests to call; then it needs to be planned according to the dates all the more. This confusion does not come from anyone making a mistake. The Hindu calendar works differently from the one on our phones. It follows the moon, and its days do not always begin and end at midnight. A festival can therefore seem to stretch across two dates on paper, even though the right day to celebrate is quite clear once you know how to read it. This year, with Diwali only a few days away, the question is back. Families are buying diyas and gifts and trying to work out when to sit down for the evening prayers. Let us read further to know when Diwali 2026 Is Diwali 2026 on November 8 or 9?
 Diwali 2026 will be celebrated on Sunday, 8 November in India, not 9 November, celebrating the main Lakshmi Puja on the day. Diwali is celebrated on Amavasya, the new moon day of the Hindu month of Kartik. The confusion kicks in when this tithi (lunar day) does not match the Gregorian calendar we follow. According to the New Delhi calendar published by Drik Panchang, Amavasya begins at 11:27 AM on 8 November and ends at 12:31 PM on 9 November. Because the tithi touches both dates, some people assume the festival could fall on either one. Happy Diwali 2026 How to know the exact date
 Lakshmi Puja is an evening ritual. It is performed during Pradosh Kaal, the period just after sunset, and the date is chosen by whichever day has Amavasya present at that time. Amavasya is present during the evening Pradosh Kaal on 8 November, so that is the day for Lakshmi Puja. On 9 November, Amavasya ends around noon, well before sunset. By the time evening comes, the tithi has already passed, and hence Diwali falls on 8th and not 9th of November. Puja timings and shubh muhurat for Diwali 2026
 According to Drik Panchang, the Lakshmi Puja muhurat will last between 5:54 PM and 7:50 PM on 8 November, and Pradosh Kaal runs from 5:31 PM to 8:09 PM. That gives a window of about 1 hour 56 minutes. Timings change from city to city because sunset is different everywhere. Drik Panchang lists, for example, Kolkata at 5:20 PM to 7:18 PM and Chennai at 6:07 PM to 8:09 PM, so it is advisable to check for your own city. Also Read: Best Rangoli Designs for Diwali 2025: Add a Touch of Tradition to Your Decor Happy Diwali 2026 Complete timeline of celebration of each day during Diwali 2026
 According to Drik Panchang, Dhanteras falls on Friday, 6 November 2026. For Choti Diwali, or Naraka Chaturdashi, Chaturdashi Tithi begins at 10:47 AM on Nov 07, 2026, and Chaturdashi Tithi ends at 11:27 AM on Nov 08, 2026. After Diwali, Govardhan Puja will be celebrated on 9 November, while Bhai Dooj will fall on the 11th of November.
